coldRead.icp: DON at a 25-bed rural hospital, reading once on a phone

undefinedTerms: 0.9 FTE per nurse on three 12s (used in the table before the post explains it two paragraphs later)
1,830 hours each FTE works after 250 hours of time off (the 2,080 starting figure only appears after the table)
your own payroll figure (which number in payroll counts as time off per FTE)
build week (read first as a verb, 'build week and posting date')
8-and-80 system 'instead' (instead of what, and what is it that 'costs more')
mondayActions: Make a ranked callout list now: charge-qualified/unit-qualified nurses not working that day, fewest hours this week first, and log each call
Count my charge-qualified nurses against 14 charge shifts a week (need at least 5) and pick one nurse to cross-train if I am at or near it
Check whether any night is covered only by LPNs, since that misses the Texas RN-on-duty rule
Before posting the next schedule, total every nurse's hours per workweek and flag any fourth 12 in a week
Pick a weekend cap number (e.g. two per four-week cycle) and start a weekend/holiday count per nurse
Set a fixed request deadline and posting date and tell the nurses
blockedActions: Post far enough ahead: no lead time is given (2, 4 or 6 weeks?), so I cannot set the posting date the Friday task asks for
Leave room for one callout shift so the first callout does not push a nurse over 40: a nurse on three 12s is at 36, so any 12-hour callout shift goes over 40; I do not know how to leave that room
Use your own payroll figure for time off: I do not know which report or which hours (PTO, sick, education, orientation) to pull

Monday count: the This Week step says divide by 36 and compare with the roster, but the table says the real answer includes time off (9.3 vs 10.6); I do not know which number to compare my roster against, or whether to compare against heads or FTEs
Confirm the Texas RN-per-building rule with your compliance lead: at my size that person may be me
